title: Spectrin
summary: Spectrin is a long, flexible protein that lines the inside of the red cell membrane. Spectrin strands join into a net, and that net is tied to proteins embedded in the membrane above it, a bit like the springs under a mattress. The net stretches and folds as the cell squeezes through a capillary, then pulls the cell back into its disc shape once it is through.
connectsUp: Spectrin is the scaffold that gives the red cell membrane both its strength and its spring.
clinical: Inherited spectrin defects are a common cause of hereditary spherocytosis, where red cells round up into fragile spheres that the spleen removes early.
